governing_text: An Extraction, the analysis of one paragraph under passages/FORMAT.md, is the source of every paragraph Move, and it is written by a fixed row on the shared supervisor with a run record rather than by a session, so that a wrong Move can be traced to the Extraction or to the ingest and the stage can be run again on the same input. [implemented-against: passages/FORMAT.md "The paragraph unit", copied 2026-10-15]

Extraction seems particularly important, so we should establish a fixed Prompt for it." The row belongs to the Proof Sheet and changes no production executable; whether a production Extractor adopts it is a separate decision.

judge.note: Every unit is a headless session, a `claude -p` child that runs with no tools (`--tools ""`), spawned by the shared Detached Job supervisor (src/workflow/detached-job.mjs). The model and both bounds NAME THE BRIEF'S SETTINGS, because the Issue gives this row the same bounds as the Brief's. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` replaces the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY.

job.note: ONE JOB PER PARAGRAPH, ONE UNIT PER JOB, run in the Leg's order, and after it the paragraph's content-bound job (kogaki#1614) and then its constraints job (kogaki#1698), on the same bounds (kogaki#1583): paragraph N's input carries the names paragraphs 1 to N-1 took, so N cannot start before N-1 is written; the state-bound job is retired with the reader table (kogaki#1699). A call past `brief.call_limit_s` is stopped and spends one attempt, a refused answer spends one, an unreadable answer is asked again without spending one, and a paragraph that has spent `brief.unit_rounds` stops the run naming the paragraph and its last refusal; the Extractions already written stay.

extraction_unit.note: The one call per paragraph (kogaki#1384). `src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs` renders this row through the shared `judgePrompt` renderer, FORMAT.md verbatim above the input marker, and the paragraph's own input below it; `validateExtractionUnit` reads the answer back against FORMAT and `extractionFileText` writes it as FORMAT's YAML record, `<name>.yaml` (kogaki#1413), so `tools/move_ingest.py passage --from-extraction` reads it unchanged through the same YAML module; `extractionMarkdown` renders the record for reading on the Proof Sheet. The fields the Harness can count or knows -- `unit`, `length`, `status` -- and each Segment's quoted `opening` words are written by the Harness, never asked.
extraction_unit.judgment_point: write the Extraction of ONE paragraph -- `paragraph_you_must_extract` in the input -- under passages/FORMAT.md, rendered above, as a PARAGRAPH-UNIT Extraction: "The paragraph unit"'s rules govern, and they override the protocol's human round -- there is no step 2, no candidate is written, and you answer Q1, Q2 and Q3 yourself, one answer each (Q4 Footing is retired, and FORMAT says why). Read `earlier_paragraphs` first (rule 2): the reader you describe has just read them. The record carries no section 2: the reader table is retired (kogaki#1699). Section 3: ONE SEGMENT PER SENTENCE, in the order of `sentences` -- the Harness has cut them, and your Segment N is sentence N. Each carries `content` -- what it does, written about this paragraph's own content -- `operation` -- the step's operation in one clause, stated subject-free, naming no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of your `subject_nouns`, so that it could be performed on any subject, and never its effect on the reader -- `relation` -- in your own prose, how the Segment relates to the one before it -- and `manner`. No label set is used for any of these fields. `manner` IS THE EMPTY STRING unless the Segment's technique is one `operation` and `relation` together cannot name: a local realisation the paragraph shows at that Segment, such as a brief direct statement that takes no elaboration, a quotation, or a shift of form. Empty is the normal case. A filled `manner` is one clause naming how the step is realised, never a point, never a reason, never a restatement of the `operation`, and it names no term, place, person or claim of the original and none of your `subject_nouns`. Segment 1's `operation` carries no reference to any earlier step or earlier paragraph. An `operation` that counts items names no number unless the number is the operation, which is the case only where the Segment sets the items against one another as a fixed set, such as a contrasting pair or the two sides of one measure: "names a counted number of parts" is the form, and "names two parts" is written only where the set is fixed (kogaki#1602). A later Segment's `operation` is the operation alone, and its `relation` carries the connection to the step before. The whole record is general: every prose field of it, `operation`, `relation`, `manner` and each entry of `breaks`, names no term, place, person or claim of the original, none of `subject_nouns`, and no word in the original's language; the record's `content` clause and `opening` are the only fields bound to the source. Rule 8: the record carries no `obligation` and no `obligation_triggers`; it carries `takes` and `leaves` instead (kogaki#1698), each a list, possibly empty, of `{ "kind", "what" }` with `kind` one of `answer` (a question raised, to be answered), `explain` (a term or item named, to be explained), `carry` (a structure given in a base, to be carried onto the subject) and `apply` (a principle, division or general statement given, to be put to work on a case or shown in an instance), and `what` one line written general, as `operation` is. `takes` is read off Segment 1: what it takes up on entry, in the terms of what an earlier paragraph could leave, and empty where Segment 1 takes nothing up. `leaves` is one entry per thing a Segment leaves for a later paragraph to take up -- a question it raises that no later Segment answers, a term it names that no later Segment explains, a base whose structure is not yet carried onto the subject, a principle not yet put to work -- each with `segment`, the number of the Segment that leaves it, and empty where the paragraph leaves nothing. No two entries of one list name the same kind and the same `what`. The Harness judges both lists against your Segments in a call of its own after this record passes. Rule 10 is retired. Rule 9: `operation`, `content`, `relation` and `manner` describe what the sentence does when read aloud. Anything the reader would know only from the page, such as emphasis, bullets, numbering, headings, line breaks or a quotation's marks, is layout: it is recorded in `passage` and nowhere else, never in `operation`, `content`, `relation` or `manner`. "Introduces a bolded term" fails the test; "introduces a term" passes it. Segment 1 carries no `relation`: its `relation` is the empty string in every paragraph, the first or a later one (rule 5), and section 1, `what_it_does`, names how the paragraph takes up the one before it. Sections 4 to 7 as FORMAT writes them; section 6, `description`, is one or two sentences telling a person reading the Move library what the paragraph does, at most 200 characters; section 7, `name`, is a snake_case verb phrase naming the transformation, not the topic, and is none of `names_taken`. Section 8, `notes`, may be empty and never carries a `split:` line: the paragraph's boundary is the source's own. Write everything in English except where you quote the paragraph.
extraction_unit.input_shape: ONE Extraction record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT, with exactly these keys: `version` "1"; `paragraph` -- the number of the paragraph in the input; `source`, `prior_text` and `language` -- FORMAT's header lines, one line each; `subject_nouns` -- an array of strings, empty for none; `answers` -- `{ "q1": <one sentence>, "q2": <one sentence>, "q3": <one sentence> }`; `what_it_does` -- section 1, one sentence; `segments` -- section 3, one entry per sentence in order, each `{ "content": <one clause>, "operation": <one clause>, "relation": <one clause, or "" on Segment 1>, "manner": <"" unless the technique is one operation and relation cannot name, otherwise one clause> }`; `takes` -- a list, possibly empty, of `{ "kind": <answer | explain | carry | apply>, "what": <one line> }`, what Segment 1 takes up; `leaves` -- a list, possibly empty, of `{ "kind": <answer | explain | carry | apply>, "what": <one line>, "segment": <the number of the Segment that leaves it> }` (kogaki#1698); `why_this_order` -- section 3's closing sentence; `presupposes` -- section 4, two or three lines as one string; `breaks` -- section 5, an array of prose tests, one or more, each one line: a specific change a careful writer might make, a dash, what the reader loses, each naming a change no other names`; `description` -- section 6, one or two sentences, at most 200 characters; `name` -- section 7; `notes` -- section 8, a string, empty for nothing. Every string is one line: no line breaks and no `|`.
extraction_unit.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; `version` not "1"; `paragraph` naming another paragraph; an empty answer or section; `segments` not one entry per sentence; a Segment missing its `content` or its `operation` clause; a Segment after the first with an empty `relation`; Segment 1 carrying a `relation`; a `manner` that restates the `operation`, adding no word of its own; a clause carrying `— operation:`, `— relation:` or `— manner:`; `breaks` not a non-empty array of one-line tests; a `subject_nouns` entry, or a word outside the Latin script, appearing in an `operation`, `relation` or `manner` clause, or a `breaks` test; a `breaks` test instructing wording or sentence order ("must open with", "must stay in one sentence" and kin: `must` or `should` before the dash) -- `breaks` informs the Composer and shape no sentence; a `description` over 200 characters; a `name` not in the library's id form (lower-case letters, digits and underscores) or already in `names_taken`; a `split:` line in `notes`; an `obligation` or `obligation_triggers` key -- retired, `leaves` names what the paragraph leaves; `takes` or `leaves` missing or not a list, an entry without `kind` or `what`, a `kind` outside answer, explain, carry and apply, an empty or multi-line `what`, a `leaves` entry without `segment` or naming a Segment the paragraph does not have, a `takes` entry carrying `segment`, two entries of one list alike in both, or a `what` naming a `subject_nouns` entry (kogaki#1698); a `takes` or `leaves` entry the constraints call judges unsupported, or a question, term, base or principle a Segment leaves that no `leaves` entry names, naming the entry or the Segment (kogaki#1698); a Segment whose `content` clause the content-bound call judges unbound -- a definite reference resolving to nothing in its sentence or `subject_nouns`, or a clause describing the sentence's act in place of its proposition -- naming the Segment and the reference (kogaki#1614); a `reader` key, the reader table being retired (kogaki#1699); a line break or a `|` in any string. Each refusal names the field, and is put back into your next attempt verbatim.
extraction_unit.governing: passages/FORMAT.md, "The paragraph unit" and "The Extraction"; kogaki#1384; kogaki#1698

content_bound_unit.note: The second call per paragraph, before the constraints call (kogaki#1614, the owner's reading of 2026-10-26). `src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs` issues it after the paragraph's Extraction record passes, and its input is the paragraph's sentences, each Segment's `content` clause beside its sentence, and `subject_nouns` as the allowed vocabulary, and nothing of the general fields: no `operation`, `relation`, `manner`, `breaks` or earlier paragraph. `validateContentBoundUnit` reads the answer back; a Segment judged unbound refuses the Extraction, and the refusal is put back into the Extractor's next attempt verbatim, within the Extractor's own attempt budget. The verdicts are written onto the record as `content_bound`, one entry per Segment. No schema file is rendered: nothing of FORMAT is this call's input.
content_bound_unit.judgment_point: judge, for EACH Segment in `segments` in the input, whether its `content` clause is BOUND to its `sentence`: whether the sentence's proposition can be reproduced from the clause alone. A clause is bound where every definite reference in it -- a phrase such as "the strongest one", "two of the countries", "this distinction", "that place" -- resolves to one of `subject_nouns` or to words of its own sentence, AND it states the sentence's proposition rather than describing the sentence's act. A clause that replaces a name the sentence gives with a description the reader cannot resolve is unbound; a clause that says what the sentence does ("the distinction matters for understanding where one country stands") in place of what it says is unbound. Judge each Segment over its own sentence and clause; you are given no other text and must infer none. Each `why` is a single line of no more than twelve words, and where `bound` is false it quotes the unresolved reference in double quotes, exactly as the clause writes it.
content_bound_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT: `{ "verdicts": [ { "bound": <true|false>, "why": <one line of at most twelve words> }, ... ] }`, one verdict per entry of `segments`, in their order. Where `bound` is false, `why` carries the unresolved reference in double quotes, copied exactly from that Segment's `content` clause. No other key. Every string is one line.
content_bound_unit.refusal: a key the answer does not declare; `verdicts` missing, or not one verdict per Segment; a verdict carrying a key other than `bound` and `why`; `bound` not true or false; `why` missing, more than one line, or over twelve words; a `why` beside `bound` false that quotes no phrase of that Segment's `content` clause in double quotes. Each refusal names the Segment, and is put back into your next attempt verbatim.
content_bound_unit.governing: passages/FORMAT.md, "The paragraph unit", rule 7 (the `content` clause is the one field bound to the source); kogaki#1614

constraints_unit.note: The third call per paragraph, in the place the obligation call held (kogaki#1698, owner ruling 2026-11-06: the constraints a Move carries are one key with two sides, `takes` and `leaves`, over four closed kinds, read by judgment). `src/proof-sheet/extract.mjs` issues it after the paragraph's Extraction record passes the content-bound call, and its input is the four kinds with their definitions (`MOVE_CONSTRAINT_KINDS` in src/move-validate.mjs), the record's `segments`, each `operation` and `relation`, and the record's `takes` and `leaves`: no Passage, no sentence, no `content` clause, no `subject_nouns`. `validateConstraintsUnit` reads the answer's shape back; an entry judged unsupported, or a thing a Segment leaves that no entry names, refuses the Extraction naming the entry or the Segment, and the refusal is put back into the Extractor's next attempt verbatim, within the Extractor's own attempt budget. `extract.mjs rejudge --constraints --library <dir>` runs the same call over an admitted library's records with the two lists null and the record's `obligation` beside its Segments, so the answer is the derived lists, and with `--write` writes them onto each record, changing no other field; `--retire-state` beside `--write` also deletes the retired `before`, `after` and `after_segment` from each record it writes (kogaki#1699). No schema file is rendered: nothing of FORMAT is this call's input.
constraints_unit.judgment_point: judge ONE Move's constraints over its own steps -- `segments` in the input, each the `operation` one sentence performs and the `relation` it bears to the sentence before -- read as the whole of the paragraph: the input holds no source text. The kinds are exactly those `kinds` gives, each with its definition: `answer`, a question raised, to be answered; `explain`, a term or item named, to be explained; `carry`, a structure given in a base, to be carried onto the subject; `apply`, a principle, division or general statement given, to be put to work on a case or shown in an instance. `takes` names what the Move's first Segment takes up on entry, in the terms of what a predecessor could leave; `leaves` names what the Move leaves for a later unit to take up, each entry with `segment`, the Segment that leaves it. WHERE THE INPUT GIVES `takes` AND `leaves`, repeat each given entry in order, its `kind`, `what` and `segment` unchanged, and give it `supported`: a `takes` entry is supported where Segment 1's `operation` takes up a thing of that kind as `what` states it, and a `leaves` entry where the Segment it names gives a thing of that kind and no later Segment answers, explains, carries or applies it. Then list in `unnamed` each question, term, base or principle a Segment leaves -- given there and not answered, explained, carried or applied by a later Segment -- that no `leaves` entry names, with its kind, a one-line `what` and the Segment; `unnamed` is empty where every such thing is named, which is the normal case. WHERE THE INPUT'S `takes` AND `leaves` ARE NULL, derive them: read the Segments, and `obligation` where the input gives it, as evidence of what the Move takes up and leaves -- an `obligation` item is a question or term left standing -- and write each entry you derive with `supported` true; `unnamed` is then empty. Both lists may be empty: a Move whose `takes` is empty can follow any unit, and one whose `leaves` is empty leaves nothing. Every `what` is one line written general, naming no term, place, person or claim of any source, and no two entries of one list name the same kind and the same `what`. Keep every `why` to twelve words on one line; for an entry you judge unsupported, it says what its Segment gives or lacks.
constraints_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT: `{ "takes": [ { "kind": <a kind>, "what": <one line>, "supported": <true|false>, "why": <one line of at most twelve words> }, ... ], "leaves": [ { "kind": <a kind>, "what": <one line>, "segment": <the 1-based number of the Segment that leaves it>, "supported": <true|false>, "why": <one line> }, ... ], "unnamed": [ { "kind": <a kind>, "what": <one line>, "segment": <number>, "why": <one line> }, ... ] }`. Where the input gives the lists, `takes` and `leaves` repeat them entry for entry; where it gives null, they are the lists you derive and `unnamed` is `[]`. No other key. Every string is one line.
constraints_unit.refusal: a key the answer does not declare; `takes`, `leaves` or `unnamed` missing or not a list; an entry missing a key or carrying one it does not declare; a `kind` outside the four; an empty or multi-line `what`; a `segment` naming a Segment the Move does not have, or a `takes` entry carrying one; two entries of one list alike in both; `supported` not true or false; `why` missing, more than one line, or over twelve words; where the input gives the lists, `takes` or `leaves` not repeating them entry for entry; where it gives null, an entry judged unsupported or `unnamed` not empty. Each refusal names the field and the entry, and is put back into your next attempt verbatim.

leg_path_unit.note: The one Leg and its Leg Waypoints (kogaki#1385, owner decision 2026-10-15). NOT AUTHORED HERE: `copy_of` names the production `reader_path_unit` row and `substitutions` the only differences, and the rendered `judgment_point` is derived from the production text at every run, so a fix to the production row reaches this one and a production edit that moves a substituted span refuses naming it. Reader start is retired (kogaki#1699): the Leg opens from the Persona's prior knowledge, given as `persona_prior_knowledge`, and carries no reader state. The Extractions stand in for Strands as the material, one Claim per paragraph; no Move is bound at the Leg level, and the Section grouping, Journey and Candidate differentiation clauses are not copied. `input_shape` and `refusal` are this row's own because the record is one Leg and not a Candidate; the refusals are the production `validateLegs` (which runs `waypointsRefusal`) over the Leg, imported, plus the one-Leg shape this row adds and the recoverability criterion over the Segment content (kogaki#1495).

substitutions.from: compose ONE CANDIDATE READER PATH for this Brief -- an ordered sequence of Legs taking the reader to the adopted Thesis, opening with the reader-state dimension and the Move the `differentiation` state assigned THIS unit (kogaki#1206), rendered above this prompt's input marker as YOUR ASSIGNED DIFFERENTIATION.
substitutions.to: compose ONE LEG for this Brief -- the original Leg whose paragraphs are `paragraphs` in the input, opening from what the Persona already knows, rendered in the input as `persona_prior_knowledge` (kogaki#1385, kogaki#1699); the Leg's `introduces` lists the terms its paragraphs define.

substitutions.from: A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699): what a Leg's Move takes up and leaves is the Move's own `takes` and `leaves`, which `moves_you_may_bind` carries per Move, read as abstract constraints and never copied into the Leg. TAKE: every Leg binds a Move whose `takes` entries are each met by an entry an earlier Leg's Move leaves and no Leg between has taken up, or, on the first Leg, by what the Persona's prior-knowledge line supplies, which the assigned opening Move's `takes` already meet -- the kinds matching as words and the `what` lines by sense, never verbatim. LEAVE: every entry a Leg's Move leaves is taken up by a later Leg's Move, or is left by the Leg marked `reaches_target` as what the article leaves the reader with, and a `carry` is never left at the end.
substitutions.to: A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699), and this Leg binds no Move, so no Move's `takes` or `leaves` is read here.

substitutions.from: The Leg marked `reaches_target` attains the Thesis (kogaki#1330), and no Opening question is rendered.
substitutions.to: The Harness marks the last Leg `reaches_target` (kogaki#1532), and no Opening question is rendered.

substitutions.from: written as this Leg's own specialization of its Move, because the Move is read here and by no stage after the Candidate.
substitutions.to: ONE LEG WAYPOINT PER PARAGRAPH OF THE ORIGINAL LEG, IN ORDER (kogaki#1385), because a Leg Waypoint is one paragraph.

substitutions.from: and it is never the Move's specialized-by-the-Leg role with the subject filled in.
substitutions.to: and Leg Waypoint N is the proposition paragraph N makes.

substitutions.from: Write the points from the Move's segments role, IN ORDER, where the library's `moves/ROLES.json` declaration maps it, and every Move carries them: a Move without `segments` is refused at the Adapter (kogaki#1320, kogaki#1349, kogaki#1412) -- a Leg may carry fewer waypoints than its Move has segments where the subject does not need them.
substitutions.to: Write the points from the paragraphs and their Extractions, IN ORDER (kogaki#1385).

substitutions.from: A reinforcing waypoint -- an example, a consequence, an answer to an objection -- names in `serves` the claim it reinforces; and a waypoint whose point no claim of the Leg supports is the signal to pull in a Journey, bind another Move, or report `no_move_fits`, never to write the waypoint anyway.
substitutions.to: THE EXTRACTIONS STAND IN FOR STRANDS (kogaki#1385): paragraph N is the material its Claim stands on, addressed `L<N>` as `claim_strand` in the input; the Leg carries ONE Claim per paragraph, and Leg Waypoint N names in `serves` the Claim of paragraph N. WHAT A PARAGRAPH SAYS AND WHAT IT DOES TO ITS READER ARE READ FROM DIFFERENT PARTS OF THE INPUT (kogaki#1480): Claim N's `proposition` and Leg Waypoint N's `point` are written from paragraph N's `text`, with its Extraction's Segment `content` clauses as that text's sentence-by-sentence reading, and carry no characterisation of the paragraph -- no "exhaustively", "exactly", "only" or "in parallel", nor any other word stating how the paragraph treats its matter rather than what it says; the Extraction's `what_it_does` is read for the Leg's `purpose` and `rationale` only, never for a `proposition` or a `point`.

substitutions.from: How many waypoints a Leg carries is yours, and you need not reproduce the Move's internal structure element for element.
substitutions.to: The Leg carries exactly as many Leg Waypoints as the original Leg has paragraphs.

substitutions.from: Two sibling units are composing the other Candidates independently over the same Brief and will not see this one's answer; the three Candidates differ BY ASSIGNMENT and not by chance, so nothing here asks a unit to guess at its siblings' choice.
substitutions.to: Bind no Move: the paragraph Move is bound per Leg Waypoint by /paragraph-plan, after the Brief (kogaki#1375).

substitutions.from: THE RENDERINGS RECORD (kogaki#1494): `renderings` in the input lists the served words this article does not keep, each with the plain phrase it uses instead, and `strand_claims` carries each Strand's served claim; a claim's `proposition` and a waypoint's `point` use a served word as served or as its declared rendering, and no third form -- a word that is neither in the served claim of the Strand it draws on, nor a declared rendering of a word in it, nor in the `introduces` of its Leg or an earlier one, nor a function word, fails the Path Review naming the word; a served word with no entry is kept as served, and no `introduces` entry carries a term the record renders, which adoption refuses.
substitutions.to: THE WORDS ARE THE SEGMENT CONTENT'S (kogaki#1495): this Brief composes no renderings record, because each paragraph's Segment `content` clauses are already the article's own rendering of its source; Claim N's `proposition` and Leg Waypoint N's `point` are written in the words of paragraph N's Segment `content` clauses -- a word that is in none of them, nor in the `introduces` of the Leg, nor a function word, is refused naming the word and the Segments.

leg_path_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `purpose`; `rationale`; `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <one sentence> }` per paragraph, in order; `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>", ...], "case": "own" | "apart" }` per paragraph, in order; and, optionally, `introduces`. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. The Harness writes `materials` (every `L<N>`) and `depends_on` (none), and no `move`, `no_move_fits`, `opens_section`, `reaches_target` or `journeys` is composed, and the Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699). `leg_ids_already_carried` lists the ids earlier Legs of this Brief carry; this Leg's `leg_id` is none of them.
leg_path_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; not exactly one Leg; a Claim count, or a Leg Waypoint count, other than the paragraph count; Claim N not naming `L<N>`, or Leg Waypoint N not serving it; and the production validators over the Leg, imported: `validateLegs` (its Leg shape, a retired reader-state field refused by name, one Claim per Strand, and `waypointsRefusal` over the Leg Waypoints) -- each refused naming the Leg and, where one is at fault, the waypoint. The Section grouping and Reader target rules are whole-path rules about where a Leg sits among others and do not bind a one-Leg Brief (kogaki#1385); and the recoverability criterion (production `recoverabilityOf`, with an empty renderings record): a word of a Claim's `proposition` or a Leg Waypoint's `point` that is in no Segment `content` of the paragraph it serves, in no `introduces` entry and is not a function word, refused naming the word and the Segments (kogaki#1495). Each refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim.
